text:
kevin: Heads-up — ACME reporting streaming aborts when clients are slow. They see partial chunks, then connection closed with EPIPE. Started after a config change to the proxy.

acme-cs: Confirmed. Happens for long SSE streams (~30m) when our UI tabs are backgrounded. The server logs show repeated "write: EAGAIN" then eventually "write: EPIPE" and client gets a 502. Billing spike noticed for same user.

maria: Can you paste the server logs and the client stacktrace? Also what proxy are you using?

acme-cs: Nginx L7 in front of the sidecar. Logs: ```
[2026-02-12T14:02:03Z] stream: write: EAGAIN (fd=73)
[2026-02-12T14:02:03Z] stream: buffering 512KB queued
[2026-02-12T14:02:05Z] stream: write: EAGAIN (fd=73)
[2026-02-12T14:02:07Z] stream: write: EPIPE (fd=73) - aborting connection
```

aj: Sounds like backpressure + proxy buffering + client paused reading. Two immediate suspects: send buffer high-water triggers in our runtime, and nginx proxy buffering causing burst writes.

kevin: Repro steps they used: 1) open SSE tab 2) leave tab backgrounded for 20–40m 3) resume tab -> see partial response and reconnect loop.

tara: Did they use chunked transfer or streaming SSE with keepalive heartbeats? Heartbeats every 15s. Client is on mobile web (Safari WKWebView).

maria: Quick test to isolate: ask them to bypass nginx (direct to sidecar on the dedicated host) and see if issue reproduces. If it doesn't, proxy is the culprit.

acme-cs: Bypassed proxy — still see slow-writer warnings but no EPIPE, connection stays open longer, client eventually catches up and resumes.

aj: That suggests proxy is applying a high-water buffer and then killing the upstream when its own buffer fills or times out. Nginx has proxy_buffering + proxy_busy_buffers_size and proxy_max_temp_file_size that can mask slow consumers and cause unexpected behavior.

kevin: What about our side — do we force abort on write failures after N retries? I recall we escalate to an abort after X consecutive EAGAINs to avoid head-of-line stalls.

maria: Yes: runtime will retry non-blocking writes up to 6 times per-chunk, then escalate to abort if writable queue exceeds 4MB and backpressure persists. This avoids OOM and preserves latency for other requests, but can disconnect slow consumers.

acme-cs: That explains the user hit. Is there a recommended config to avoid disconnects but also not blow up server memory?

aj: Options: 1) Reduce proxy buffering so backpressure propagates more smoothly (proxy_buffering off for SSE). 2) Increase socket send buffer and our per-connection high-water limit for long-lived SSE but with a safety cap. 3) Enable smaller keepalive heartbeats so client wakes and drains. 4) Add a disk-backed temp buffer on proxy (not ideal for latency).

tara: Also check TCP_NODELAY and disable Nagle on sidecar sockets — small intermittent writes may be coalesced and cause larger bursts when the client unblocks.

kevin: For immediate customer workaround, recommend disabling proxy buffering for their SSE route and lowering proxy timeout to avoid long buffering. Will send step-by-step.

maria: Can you also capture a server pcap around the event? We want to see the TCP window size and retransmits. If we have pcap + logs we can decide whether to relax our high-water limit.

acme-cs: Uploading a small pcap now. Also, they noted a billing anomaly where token accounting showed repeated short reconnects generating many small billing events.

aj: That billing effect is expected if client reconnects without resuming token offset — each reconnect can create a new billable session. We should add guidance to resume tokens on reconnect or to suppress billing for immediate reconnects within a short window (feature ask).

kevin: Action list: @maria will draft proxied SSE config recommendations; @aj will create a repro harness that simulates a backgrounded slow reader; tara will look at socket options and our high-water thresholds; kevin will reply to customer with workaround and ask for pcap + timestamps.

maria: Draft config snippet for nginx: ```
location /events/ {
  proxy_pass http://sidecar;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
  proxy_set_header Connection '';
  tcp_nodelay on;
}
```

tara: Repro notes for the harness: use tc qdisc netem to pause RX on the client for 30–60s, then resume. Observe server queued bytes and count of EAGAIN. I'll post results.

aj: If we change high-water limits, make it configurable per-tenant so Dedicated customers can opt-in to higher per-connection buffers. Otherwise default stays conservative.

kevin: Good. I'll file a support ticket with the suggested immediate changes and tag platform for follow-up on per-tenant buffering configuration. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy/monitoring: New dashboard panel created: "sse-slow-consumer-eagain" (alerts: rate > 5/min over 5m).
